report_name: Critical cPanel Flaw Allows Hosting Customers to Gain Root Access

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: An authenticated, low-privileged user can exploit the cPanel & WHM software, which is a public-facing application for hosting customers, to gain initial access to the server's filesystem beyond their intended permissions.

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: The vulnerability allows a low-privilege authenticated cPanel user to escalate privileges to the root user by writing arbitrary files to sensitive locations on the server.

attack_patterns.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Cron
attack_patterns.description: An attacker can exploit the vulnerability to write a malicious cron job to a directory like '/etc/cron.d/', which will then be executed with root privileges, leading to server compromise.

attack_patterns.name: Account Manipulation: SSH Authorized Keys
attack_patterns.description: An attacker can exploit the vulnerability to add their own public SSH key to the root user's '/root/.ssh/authorized_keys' file, allowing them to log in directly as root via SSH.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-65643
vulnerabilities.description: A critical path traversal or insufficient validation flaw in cPanel & WHM's domain parking functionality allows an authenticated user to write arbitrary files on the server, leading to code execution as the root user.

identities.name: cPanel
identities.description: The vendor of the cPanel & WHM web hosting control panel software that contains the CVE-2026-65643 vulnerability.

indicators.name: cPanel Suspicious Domain Parking Activity
indicators.pattern:
title: cPanel Suspicious Domain Parking Activity
id: 2b1a3c4d-5e6f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects suspicious POST requests to cPanel scripts related to domain parking that may indicate exploitation of CVE-2026-65643.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-28
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/critical-cpanel-flaw-could-let-one.html
tags:
  - attack.t1190
level: high
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: 'POST'
    c-uri|contains|all:
      - '/json-api/cpanel'
      - 'api_func=park'
    c-uri|contains:
      - '../'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects suspicious POST requests to cPanel's domain parking scripts containing directory traversal sequences, which could indicate an attempt to exploit CVE-2026-65643.

indicators.name: Suspicious File Creation in Cron Directory
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious File Creation in Cron Directory
id: 8d7c6b5a-4f3e-4d2c-1b0a-9e8f7d6c5b4a
status: experimental
description: 'Detects the creation of new files in cron directories, which could be a result of exploiting CVE-2026-65643 to establish persistence.'
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-28
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/critical-cpanel-flaw-could-let-one.html
tags:
  - attack.t1053.003
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - '/etc/cron.d/'
      - '/var/spool/cron/'
  filter_legit:
    Image:
      - '/usr/bin/crontab'
      - '/usr/sbin/anacron'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
indicators.description: Detects the creation of files in system cron directories by unexpected processes, a potential indicator of persistence established via CVE-2026-65643.

indicators.name: Suspicious Modification of Root SSH Authorized Keys
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Modification of Root SSH Authorized Keys
id: 5a4b3c2d-1e0f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: 'Detects modification of the root user''s authorized_keys file, which could indicate an attacker adding their key for persistent root access via CVE-2026-65643.'
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-28
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/critical-cpanel-flaw-could-let-one.html
tags:
  - attack.t1098.004
level: critical
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename: '/root/.ssh/authorized_keys'
  filter_legit:
    Image:
      - '/usr/bin/ssh-copy-id'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
indicators.description: Detects modifications to the root user's SSH authorized_keys file, a strong indicator of compromise if performed by an unexpected process like a web server, potentially via CVE-2026-65643.
